recommended_title: Response Ceilings and Targeted Investment in Multitask Leaderboards
central_question: Under a bounded, target-only score-response model with fixed rivals, how many task coordinates must be improved to attain strict first place, and how does that investment depend on the aggregation rule and response ceiling?
central_thesis: In the evaluated public score panels, aggregation robustness is conditional on the response ceiling: exact six-task results reverse the mean–median minimum-support ordering between half and full headroom on matched attainable targets, while larger subject-level panels establish feasible investment bounds rather than exact rule rankings.
narrative_rationale: This is a bounded counterfactual empirical study, not a new optimizer or training study. Existing final decision records support a direct rule-by-response comparison, including an exact matched-cohort reversal on the six-task Open LLM panel and explicit uncertainty about optimal support on the 57-subject HELM panel. The same scientific question organizes these as complementary evidence blocks with different certificate strength, not as transfer or discovery-order experiments. The frozen reference procedure is the studied method; unsuccessful search proposals are not the contribution. No universal ordering, practical training cost, or causal contamination effect is inferred.
edit_framing_decision: No edit context, previous_paper directory, prior manuscript, aggregated directory, or extra_tasks directory is staged. The rejected status denotes rejection of an assumed inherited improvement story, not rejection of an actual manuscript. Compare three alternatives explicitly: preserve an optimizer-improvement story, broaden to a shared novel certificate family, or recenter on response-dependent investment comparisons. Choose the third: no search improvement was selected, component ablations are absent, and exact rule contrasts are stronger than claims of algorithmic novelty.
staged_input_impact: Directly inspected source_evidence/downstream/program/src/program.py and the baseline counterpart; their source files are identical. The selected procedure exhausts panels with at most six coordinates, uses sorted headroom for larger mean panels, and marginal-score greedy supports for larger median and trimmed-mean panels.
Read final_evaluation independently of downstream_study. Its completed, qualified evaluation supports a finished empirical study; it does not establish population generalization or solver novelty.

The ordinary primary six-task records contain exact support outcomes, whereas the 57-subject median and trimmed-mean records retain bounded support outcomes. This changes the center of gravity from solver improvement to aggregation sensitivity with explicit certificate scope.
The separate auxiliary BBH and six-coordinate projections add sensitivity and verification depth, not a new architecture, new model training condition, or a pooled primary benchmark.
The local ICLR style is single-column, with a 5.5-inch text width and 9-inch text height. This supports full-text-width, low-density comparisons rather than two-column dashboard figures.

The supplied bibliography contains metadata retrieval records, many tangential to this study, without evidence of substantive reading. Its presence does not license scientific positioning or citation padding. No external source was accessed during strategy generation.

method_groups.name: Frozen bounded-headroom support-minimization procedure
method_groups.include_reason: This is the selected studied procedure, not a newly successful proposal: improve selected coordinates by alpha times their remaining headroom, hold rivals fixed, and report exact support, certified infeasibility, or an honest lower–upper support interval. Explain exhaustive small-panel search, exact mean sorting, and larger-panel greedy witnesses separately.

method_groups.name: Equal-task arithmetic mean
method_groups.include_reason: Provides the directly grounded aggregation comparator and an analytically exact sorted-headroom solution; retain it in every main rule comparison.

method_groups.name: Conventional median
method_groups.include_reason: The central exact six-task contrast uses the conventional median, including the average of the two middle values for an even task count; distinguish this from a lower or upper median.

method_groups.name: Symmetric 20-percent trimmed mean
method_groups.include_reason: Provides the grounded intermediate order-statistic condition: remove floor(m/5) values from each tail. It checks whether the evidence is specific to the median without extending to untested ordinal rules.

method_groups.name: No-intervention, seeded-random, and marginal-score-greedy investment policies
method_groups.include_reason: These comparators already have matched final decision records. They contextualize support selection, retain zero and negative differences, and show that the selected procedure coincides with greedy in important regimes. They are not component ablations or independent model-training methods.

results_focus: Primary thesis test: ordinary Open LLM primary decisions only; match by seed and target slot and retain targets attainable under both mean and median at alpha=0.5 and alpha=1.0. Compare exact support fractions on that identical per-seed cohort across both response conditions. The recorded data give a negative median-minus-mean average at half headroom and a positive average at full headroom for every final seed. This is a descriptive within-snapshot reversal, not a pre-registered significance claim.

Report attainability for all sampled ordinary primary targets at alpha=0.25, 0.5, and 1.0, separately for HELM and Open LLM, so conditioning the exact contrast on attainable cases cannot conceal infeasible targets.

Report support cost with exactness attached: exact support for the six-task panel and the mean, but evaluator lower bounds and selected feasible upper bounds for larger median/trimmed panels. A reversal of greedy witness costs on HELM must not be called a reversal of minimum costs when bound intervals overlap.

Retain matched policy comparisons, preferably a compact main table at alpha=0.5 and the complete grid after references. State where exact selection reduces support relative to greedy and where it ties. Existing paired intervals compare the selected procedure against random or greedy; they are not cross-rule confidence intervals.

Keep constant-ceiling, zero-response, permutation, and replay checks separate from ordinary performance. A passed check establishes only the property tested, not universal scientific validity or optimality.

Use auxiliary six-coordinate projections and revision-matched BBH decisions only as separately labeled sensitivity evidence. Do not merge them with primary scores, compare their target slots as identical model identities, or claim domain transfer.
figure_plan: Figure 1, early overview: fixed public task scores and rivals; target-only bounded-headroom intervention; three aggregation rules leading to exact support, infeasibility, or an interval. No fabricated score matrix or illustrative numerical result.

Figure 2, central exact comparison: two matched-cohort dot plots, one for half headroom and one for full headroom, showing median-minus-mean minimum-support fraction by final sampling seed with a zero reference line.

Figure 3, scope and cost: a 2-by-2 composite with one row per primary panel family, all-target attainability at three response ceilings on the left, and paired attainable-cohort support bounds at half/full headroom on the right. Exact values and unresolved intervals use visibly different marks.

Use tables, not additional main figures, for snapshot scope, comparator differences, and certificate/status counts. Put the full conditional comparator-interval grid and auxiliary sensitivities after references.

figure_specs.purpose: Make the counterfactual investment object, fixed-rival assumption, aggregation conditions, and certificate outcomes legible before quantitative results.
figure_specs.split_by: fixed scores, bounded intervention, aggregation and support outcome
figure_specs.layout_rationale: In the inspected single-column ICLR style, full width is 5.5 inches, not a two-column spread. Use a shallow approximately 5.5-by-1.8-inch diagram on page 1 or 2; a half-width 2.75-inch rendering would compress the update equation and outcome labels. Keep at most six visual groups and three aggregator branches, with at least 9-point rendered labels.
figure_specs.content_constraints: Show x_j changing to x_j+alpha(1-x_j) only on the selected support and label rivals fixed. Three aggregators are conditions, not sequential improvements. Distinguish exact, infeasible, and bounded outcomes. Do not draw training, an architecture transition, a novel certificate mechanism, or numerical toy measurements.

figure_specs.purpose: Display the exact within-snapshot mean–median ordering reversal without infeasibility penalties, composition changes across response conditions, or search chronology.
figure_specs.metric: mean exact median-minus-mean support fraction on a fixed jointly attainable cohort
figure_specs.split_by: alpha=0.5 versus alpha=1.0 on the ordinary Open LLM primary panel
figure_specs.layout_rationale: Two side-by-side panels occupy approximately 5.5 by 2.1 inches in the 5.5-inch single text column. Each panel has three seed categories and one contrast series, so 9-point labels and a common signed y scale remain readable; include a horizontal zero line and cohort counts in the caption. Do not connect response conditions as a time trajectory.
figure_specs.content_constraints: Filter ordinary primary Open LLM decisions, join rule/alpha cells by seed and slot, and intersect attainability under both rules at both response conditions. Each seed retains the same cohort in both panels. Plot exact support-count differences divided by six; show individual seed summaries, not invented confidence intervals or a pooled population p-value.

figure_specs.purpose: Show which targets can attain first place and how much support is established, while exposing differences between exact and bounded evidence.
figure_specs.metric: left: target attainment rate; right: normalized support lower and feasible upper bounds
figure_specs.split_by: HELM 57-subject panel versus Open LLM six-task panel
figure_specs.layout_rationale: A 2-by-2 figure at approximately 5.5 by 3.4 inches uses the full single-column width. Two panels per row, three ceiling categories at most, three rule series, shared scales, and a common legend avoid shrinking a dashboard. Use at least 9-point final labels and a short caption explicitly defining the support cohorts and interval semantics.
figure_specs.content_constraints: Left panels include every ordinary primary target at all three recorded ceilings and use one attainment definition: a verified strict-first support with a supported claim. Right panels use only alpha=0.5 and 1.0, intersect attainable targets across all three rules within each seed and ceiling, and report the cohort sizes. Average the within-seed lower and upper support fractions with declared equal seed weights; the interval is an identification/certification range, not a confidence interval. Cohorts here may differ across ceilings, unlike Figure 2. Exact costs collapse to points. Never draw the infeasible sentinel m+1 as an actual cost. If a required joint cohort is empty, show not estimable rather than imputation.

notes_for_writer: Format contract: target the provided ICLR 2026 single-column style and anonymized review format. The inspected paper.sty declares textwidth 5.5in and textheight 9in. Here preferred_span=full_width means the one full text column; a column-width two-column convention does not apply. Do not replace the venue with the NeurIPS template mentioned in source-task provenance.

Body plan: aim for about 8.5 substantive pages, excluding references: 1.25 pages for abstract/introduction and contribution scope, 0.75 for safely grounded related work and modeling context, 1.0 for objective/assumptions, 1.0 for solver and certificate scope, 0.75 for experimental protocol and uncertainty, 2.75 for exact contrast/attainability/support/comparators including figures, and 1.0 for limitations and conclusion. Figure area is included, not added on top. An eight-page body must fill at least 75 percent of its last page; never pad to reach this threshold.

Suggested thesis-first headings: Introduction; Related Work and Scope; Bounded-Response Investment; Computing Support and Certifying Limits; Public Score Panels and Comparison Protocol; Response-Dependent Aggregation Costs; Attainability and Certificate Scope; Limitations and Conclusion. No campaign-order sections.

Define x in [0,1], selected support S, target update x_j+alpha(1-x_j) for j in S, fixed competitors, and unique first as aggregate(target)>max rival aggregate+1e-10. Investment is |S|, normalized by panel task count for cross-panel display. Total normalized score lift is secondary and is not training examples, compute, dollars, or contamination severity. Alpha is a stipulated response fraction, not an estimated learning curve.

State equal task weighting, no spillover or regression on untouched coordinates, fixed rival pool, and score normalization explicitly. A support-cardinality comparison across six tasks and 57 subjects does not equate their real-world intervention costs. Avoid interpreting named architectures or task metadata as controlled architecture experiments.
